## Appearance

Uncle Jim is a homely, tall, and ungainly man with spare jaws, a rugged mouth, and a square brow. He has a deeply lined, bronzed face, clear and deep-set blue eyes, and a thick mane of iron-gray hair that falls to his shoulders. Over time, his hair grows much grayer, and he eventually appears frail and bent.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Uncle Jim is a simple-minded, high-souled old man who possesses an invariably placid and cheerful demeanor. A passionate worshipper of beauty, he derives a deep, inner joy from every lovely thing he sees or hears. He is a talented storyteller and fiddler, though he harbors a deep dread of experiencing a lingering death.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 8 MISS CORNELIA BRYANT COMES TO CALL P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P9](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0009), [v4 CHAPTER 17 A FOUR WINDS WINTER P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), +1 more_

## History

As a young man, Captain Jim ran off to sea, driven by his maternal seafaring heritage, and he spent many years sailing aboard the Gray Gull alongside his old crony Henry Pollack. Although he had no children of his own, he bore the enduring loss of his childhood sweetheart, [Margaret](../character/margaret.md), who had tragically drifted away at sea over fifty years prior. Decades after these early adventures, he welcomed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) upon their arrival in [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), quickly recognizing [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) as a kindred spirit and establishing a close friendship with the couple. He routinely entertained visitors at the [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) lighthouse with his collection of curiosities and extensive sea tales, while also remaining a steady pillar of the community by escorting [Dick Moore](../character/dick-moore.md) home to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and providing financial assistance through a mortgage so [Dick](../character/dick-moore.md) could undergo surgery in [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal). When [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md) visited the harbor, Captain Jim discovered that Owen was the grandson of his old schoolmaster’s bride; he subsequently lent Owen his personal life-book, which Owen adapted into a finished novel incorporating Margaret's memory. Later, Captain Jim gave his heartfelt benediction to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and Owen after they confessed their mutual love, and he asked [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to care for his cat, [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md), as he contemplated his mortality. Shortly after receiving the very first printed copy of his published life story from [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), Captain Jim passed away peacefully overnight on his sofa while reading its final pages.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P0](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0000), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P7](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0007), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P16](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0016), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P31](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0031), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P34](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0034), +38 more_

## Quotes

> "Nephew Alec. He understands it as well as I do. Well, now, I’m real glad you asked me to stay to supper. I’m proper hungry—didn’t have much of a dinner today."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P19](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0019)

> “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0021)

> "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P24](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0024)

> "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)

> "Yes, I called in on my way home to see him. He’s getting round all right—but stewing in a broth of trouble, as usual, poor man."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 18 SPRING DAYS P29](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0029)
